name: Fujitsu SPARC64 VIIIfx with HPC-ACE
description: Fujitsu built an eight-core processor for the K computer. Its HPC-ACE extensions to SPARC V9 added operations for parallel floating-point arithmetic and a larger register set for scientific workloads.

date.basis: Fujitsu's corporate chronology dates the debut to May 2009.

events.statement: Fujitsu publicly introduced the SPARC64 VIIIfx at Fujitsu Forum.

evidence.supports: Identifies the processor and month of the public debut.

date.basis: The Hot Chips presentation is dated 25 August.

events.statement: Fujitsu presented the eight-core VIIIfx, its HPC-ACE instructions and hardware results from a working chip.

evidence.supports: Names the chip, describes HPC-ACE and presents results measured on hardware.

earliest_record.rationale: Fujitsu records a May 2009 public debut and its August presentation provides technical detail.

unresolved.note: Maruyama identifies SPARC64 VII design reuse as a development target and contrasts the pipelines. Which microarchitectural blocks can be traced to VII with independently informative evidence?

links.statement: The SPARC64 VIIIfx implements the SPARC V9 instruction architecture through JPS1 Commonality. Fujitsu’s HPC-ACE adds floating-point SIMD and extends the register set for scientific computing.
links.scope: Instruction-set lineage, via JPS1, for the processor used in K.

evidence.supports: Specifies the base SPARC V9 instruction and register architecture.
The separately issued joint common specification directly derives from the SPARC V9 manual.
The VIIIfx implementation specification explicitly uses the JPS1 common definitions and names the processor a SPARC V9 implementation.
The designer identifies V9 and JPS as standards used, and describes the HPC-ACE register and SIMD additions.
